verdict.rationale:
Crossplane's core resources (Providers, Compositions, Managed Resources) are defined declaratively in YAML, but its Composition Functions pipeline lets you write configuration logic in general-purpose languages like Python and Go (as well as KCL), which brings programmatic constructs into part of the workflow. This falls short of a full GPL-based IaC experience with native types, loops, and IDE support across the whole resource model as in tools like Pulumi/CDK.
missing for 10: evidence of typed SDKs for defining Crossplane resources natively in Go/Python/TypeScript with IDE autocomplete, evidence of loop/conditional constructs used to generate multiple resources, and independent hands-on confirmation of IDE tooling quality.
